Score location surfaces against known positions

score_surfaces.Rd

For simulated animals, whose true positions are known, measures how far each location surface lies from the truth and whether its credible region holds the truth. The truth of an animal-bin is every transmission the animal sent in the bin: the transmissions are joined to the bins by animal_id and time, bin_start <= datetime < bin_end.

Usage

score_surfaces(surfaces, truth, level = 0.95)

Arguments

surfaces

Location surfaces from detfield::location_surface().

truth

The true transmissions: a data frame with animal_id, datetime (POSIXct, UTC, no NA), x and y in the CRS of the surfaces' grid, such as simulate_transmissions() returns or the transmissions element of simulate_detections().

level

Share of the probability the credible region holds; above 0 and at most the kept mass of the surfaces.

Value

A list of class surface_score with three data frames:

  • bins: one row per animal-bin, with animal_id, bin_start, n_truth (transmissions in the bin), truth_x, truth_y, mode_x, mode_y, mean_x, mean_y, error_mode_m, error_mean_m, in_region, area_m2 and region_mass.

  • animals: one row per animal, with n_bins and the summaries below.

  • overall: one row, with n_animals, n_bin_starts, n_bins, the summaries below, mean_region_mass, hit_rate_se, hit_rate_se_from, hit_rate_df, hit_rate_lo, hit_rate_hi, hit_rate_se_animal and hit_rate_se_bins.

The summaries are median_error_mode_m, p90_error_mode_m, median_error_mean_m, p90_error_mean_m, hit_rate and median_area_m2. Attributes: level, and no_truth, the number of bins left out because no transmission of the animal fell in them.

Details

Per animal-bin:

  • error_mode_m and error_mean_m: the distance from the centre of the surface's most probable cell, and from the probability-weighted mean of its cell centres, to the centroid of the bin's transmission positions.

  • in_region: the share of the bin's transmissions that fall in a cell of the credible region at level. For an animal that stays in one cell for the bin, as the likelihood assumes, this is 0 or 1; an animal that moves across the region's edge in the bin scores in between.

  • area_m2 and region_mass: the area of the credible region and the probability it holds. A region is whole cells, so it holds at least level; compare the hit rate with the mean mass as well as with the level.

Hit rate. The hit rate is the mean of in_region over bins, so each bin counts once: the share of the truth that the credible regions hold. It checks whether the regions are as wide as their level says. Compare designs on the error and the scored share. When animals move within the hour it falls as the regions shrink, so a denser array scores lower; see evaluate_array().

Bins share an animal, and animals share an hour: a receiver that hears badly in one hour does so for every animal. hit_rate_se is therefore clustered two ways, by animal and by bin start (Cameron, Gelbach and Miller 2011, doi:10.1198/jbes.2010.07136 ): sqrt(V_a + V_t - V_b), where V_a and V_t are the one-way cluster variances, each G / (G - 1) * sum_g r_g^2 / N^2 with r_g the summed residuals of cluster g, G the clusters and N the bins, and V_b the same over single bins. A way with one cluster drops out. The result is never taken below the larger one-way SE, a conservative floor chosen here: the subtraction can pull the two-way value under both when one way carries no correlation, and the paper's own fallback for a negative value is the larger one-way SE. hit_rate_se_from says which estimate was used: "animal and bin start", "animal (floor)" or "bin start (floor)"; "animal" or "bin start" when the other way has one cluster; "not estimable" when every bin scores the same; NA for one bin. hit_rate_se_animal clusters by animal only and hit_rate_se_bins treats bins as independent; both are too small when bins share an hour's detection conditions.

The 95% interval hit_rate_lo to hit_rate_hi uses the t distribution with hit_rate_df degrees of freedom, the smaller cluster count less one, the small-sample adjustment Cameron, Gelbach and Miller (2011) use because the SE rests on few clusters. With few bin starts, such as the six hours of evaluate_array()'s defaults, the SE itself is noisy and the interval is rough. The script that measures how often it holds, https://github.com/jakebrownscombe/arraydesign/blob/main/validation/02_scoring_validation.R, is in the repository and not in the installed package. When every bin scores the same, the SE cannot be estimated: hit_rate_se is NA and, at a hit rate of 0 or 1, the interval is the exact binomial bound for that many successes or failures in as many trials as the smaller cluster count.

See also

evaluate_array(), which simulates, positions and scores in one call.

Examples

stoney <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                  package = "arraydesign"))
planned <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "planned_stations.csv",
                                package = "arraydesign"))
rx <- place_receivers(stoney, method = "manual", coords = planned)
range_model <- detfield::de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500),
                                     depth = c(1, 35))
# Pairs more than 4 km apart through water are left out. At the deepest
# receiver the curve gives them a detection probability below 1e-7, and
# the distances take a third of the time.
field <- detfield::de_field(detfield::water_distances(stoney, rx, max_distance = 4000),
                            range_model)
#> 52 of 2,304 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.
# Five animals for 3 hours each.
tr <- simulate_tracks(stoney, crw_model(30, 15, 40, time_step_s = 60),
                      n_animals = 5, n_steps = 180, seed = 1)
tx <- simulate_transmissions(tr, tag_delay = c(120, 180), seed = 2)
det <- simulate_detections(tx, field, overdispersion = "none", seed = 3)
listening <- data.frame(receiver_serial = rx$receiver_serial,
                        date = as.Date("2025-01-01"))
counts <- detfield::bin_detections(det$detections, listening,
                                   tag_delay = c(120, 180))
surfaces <- detfield::location_surface(counts, field, overdispersion = "none")
score <- score_surfaces(surfaces, det$transmissions)
score
#> <surface_score> 7 animal-bins of 4 animals; 95% credible regions
#>   error of the mode: median 511 m, 90th percentile 1229 m
#>   error of the mean: median 365 m, 90th percentile 597 m
#>   hit rate 0.621: share of the truth inside the 95% regions (a calibration
#>     check)
#>     95% interval 0.000 to 1.000 (SE 0.170 clustered by bin start, the
#>       one-way floor; 4 animals and 3 bin starts; t with 2 df); regions hold
#>       0.952 on average
#>   median region 650,000 m^2
